description: Fields, waves, transmission lines, antennas and radio-frequency circuits, from Maxwell's equations to a working link budget. Students solve fields numerically, match lines on the Smith chart, design signal-integrity fixes on the circuit bench and size radio links for rural Africa.
modelledOn: Balanis, Antenna Theory: Analysis and Design
Johnson and Graham, High-Speed Digital Design
outcomes: Apply vector calculus and Maxwell's equations to static fields, plane waves and boundary problems.
Analyse transmission lines with reflection coefficient, VSWR, bounce diagrams and the Smith chart, and design matching networks.
Diagnose and fix signal-integrity problems on fast digital interconnects using termination, stackup and decoupling.
Characterise antennas by pattern, gain and impedance, and design simple dipoles, arrays and patches.
Build a link budget with a propagation model and decide whether a radio link in a given terrain will work.
Analyse RF chains for gain, noise and nonlinearity, and apply shielding and filtering for electromagnetic compatibility.

units.title: Vector fields and static fields
topics: Vector calculus review: gradient, divergence, curl in Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates
Electrostatics: Coulomb's law, Gauss's law, potential and capacitance
Laplace and Poisson equations; numerical solution by finite differences
Magnetostatics: Biot-Savart law, Ampere's law, flux and inductance
Materials and boundary conditions: dielectrics, conductors and magnetic media

units.title: Maxwell's equations and plane waves
topics: Faraday's law, displacement current and the four Maxwell equations in integral and differential form
The wave equation and uniform plane waves in lossless media; phase velocity and wave impedance
Waves in lossy media and good conductors; attenuation and skin depth
Polarisation: linear, circular and elliptical; polarisation loss
Power flow and the Poynting vector
Reflection and transmission at a dielectric interface: normal and oblique incidence, Snell's law, Brewster angle

units.title: Transmission lines and the Smith chart
topics: Distributed circuit model and the telegrapher's equations; characteristic impedance and propagation constant
Lossless and low-loss lines; reflection coefficient, standing waves and VSWR
Input impedance, the quarter-wave transformer and open and short stubs
The Smith chart: impedance and admittance, moving along a line
Impedance matching with single-stub and lumped L-networks
Transients on lines: step response and the bounce (lattice) diagram

units.title: Signal integrity for high-speed digital design
topics: When an interconnect is a transmission line: edge rate versus trace length
Microstrip and stripline impedance, PCB stackup and return paths
Termination schemes: series, parallel and Thevenin; reflections and ringing
Crosstalk, ground bounce and simultaneous switching noise
Decoupling, power integrity, eye diagrams and jitter

units.title: Waveguides, resonators and optical fibre
topics: Rectangular waveguide: TE and TM modes and cutoff frequency
Dispersion, phase and group velocity in guided waves
Cavity resonators and quality factor
Planar lines: microstrip, coplanar waveguide and substrate choice
Optical fibre as a dielectric waveguide: modes, attenuation, dispersion

units.title: Antennas
topics: Radiation from a current element; radiation pattern, beamwidth, directivity, gain and efficiency
Half-wave dipole and monopole: pattern, input impedance and bandwidth
Antenna arrays: array factor, element spacing, grating lobes and beam steering
Aperture antennas: horn and parabolic reflector; gain and illumination efficiency
Microstrip patch antennas: design equations, feeding and bandwidth
Antenna measurement, polarisation matching and Sub-Saharan deployments: VHF/UHF masts, rural 4G and VSAT dishes

units.title: Propagation and link budgets
topics: Free-space propagation: the Friis equation, EIRP and path loss
Terrestrial models: two-ray ground reflection, log-distance and empirical macro-cell models
Fading and shadowing: Rayleigh and Rician fading, fade margin
Line-of-sight microwave links: Fresnel zones, earth bulge, tower height and rain attenuation
Satellite links: G/T, noise temperature and Eb/N0
Link budget design and rural coverage planning: cell radius, TV white space and community networks

units.title: RF circuits and systems
topics: Two-port networks and S-parameters; reading a vector network analyser plot
Noise figure and the Friis cascade formula; receiver sensitivity
Low-noise and power amplifiers: gain, stability and matching
Mixers, local oscillators and the superheterodyne receiver; image frequency
Filters (LC, coupled-line) and nonlinearity: 1 dB compression and third-order intercept

units.title: Electromagnetic compatibility
topics: Sources and victims of interference; conducted and radiated emissions
Coupling mechanisms: common impedance, capacitive, inductive and radiative
Shielding effectiveness, apertures and cable shields
Grounding, filtering and ferrites; lightning and surge protection for tropical installations
EMC standards and pre-compliance testing practice

schedule.title: Vector fields and static fields
schedule.exercise: Use Gauss's law to find the field of a charged sphere and a line charge, and solve Laplace's equation by hand for a parallel-plate capacitor with one dielectric layer.

tasks.title: Plot a given 2D vector field, compute its divergence and curl symbolically, and mark the regions of positive divergence on the plot
Solve Laplace's equation on a 20 by 20 grid by Gauss-Seidel iteration for a coaxial cross-section and compare the capacitance with the analytic value
Apply boundary conditions at a dielectric interface to find the refracted field angle, and plot how flux density bends for permittivity ratios 1 to 10

schedule.title: Maxwell's equations and plane waves
schedule.exercise: State the four Maxwell equations and the physical law behind each, derive the wave equation in free space, and compute the skin depth of copper at 1 MHz and 2.4 GHz.

tasks.title: Plot E and H of a 100 MHz plane wave in free space against position and time, and read off wavelength, phase velocity and wave impedance
Compute attenuation and skin depth for copper, seawater and moist soil from 1 kHz to 10 GHz, and plot the results on a log scale
Simulate a pulse entering a lossy medium with a finite-difference 1D FDTD loop and measure the pulse amplitude after 1, 2 and 3 skin depths

schedule.title: Polarisation and reflection at interfaces
schedule.exercise: Find reflection and transmission coefficients for a wave going from air to glass at several angles, and decide whether a given pair of antennas suffers polarisation loss.

tasks.title: Plot the tip of E for linear, circular and elliptical polarisation from given amplitudes and phase, and compute the axial ratio
Plot reflection coefficient against incidence angle for parallel and perpendicular polarisation on glass, and locate the Brewster angle
Compute average Poynting power for a wave crossing a layered slab and verify that reflected plus transmitted power equals incident power at every angle

schedule.title: Transmission line theory
schedule.exercise: Derive Z0 for a lossless line from its per-unit-length L and C, then compute the reflection coefficient, VSWR and input impedance of a 75 ohm line terminated in 50 ohms.

tasks.title: Compute Z0, phase velocity and wavelength for a coaxial line and a two-wire line from their dimensions and permittivity, and tabulate the results
Drive a lossless line model with a sine source, vary the load, and measure VSWR from the voltage envelope for short, open, matched and 100 ohm loads
Design a quarter-wave transformer to match a 100 ohm load to a 50 ohm line at 900 MHz and plot return loss against frequency

schedule.title: Smith chart, matching and transients
schedule.exercise: Match a complex load of 30 + j40 ohms to a 50 ohm line with a single stub, and draw the bounce diagram for a step applied to a mismatched line.

tasks.title: Plot four given load impedances on a Smith chart, read each reflection coefficient and move 0.125 wavelengths toward the generator
Find the stub length and position that match a given complex load to 50 ohms, and verify return loss better than 30 dB at the design frequency
Apply a 5 V step to a mismatched line in the circuit bench and capture the staircase waveform, then confirm it against the bounce diagram you drew

schedule.title: Signal integrity
schedule.exercise: Estimate the critical trace length for a 1 ns edge on FR4, choose a termination for a point-to-point clock line, and list three layout changes that reduce crosstalk.

tasks.title: Compute the trace length at which a line must be treated as a transmission line for rise times of 5 ns, 1 ns and 200 ps on FR4
Drive a 50 ohm trace with a fast clock into a CMOS input, observe ringing, then add series termination and measure overshoot before and after
Model two coupled traces with mutual capacitance and inductance, measure near-end crosstalk against spacing, and find the spacing that keeps it below 5 percent

schedule.title: Waveguides, resonators and fibre
schedule.exercise: Compute the cutoff frequencies of the first five modes of a standard rectangular waveguide, find the resonant frequencies of a cavity, and compute the loss of a 20 km fibre link.

tasks.title: Compute cutoff frequencies of TE and TM modes for a WR-90 waveguide and list which modes propagate at 10 GHz and 15 GHz
Plot phase and group velocity against frequency for a rectangular waveguide, and confirm the product of the two equals the square of the speed of light
Build the power budget for a 20 km single-mode fibre link with splices and connectors, and test if the received power exceeds receiver sensitivity

schedule.title: Antenna fundamentals and the dipole
schedule.exercise: Compute directivity and effective area from a given radiation pattern, and sketch the E-plane and H-plane patterns for a half-wave dipole and a quarter-wave monopole.

tasks.title: Plot the polar pattern of a half-wave dipole, read its half-power beamwidth, and estimate directivity by numerical integration of the pattern
Compute input impedance of a dipole as its length varies from 0.25 to 1 wavelength, and find the length for resonance at 145 MHz
Compute the array factor of an N-element uniform linear array in code, and find element spacing and phase shift that steer the main beam to 30 degrees

schedule.title: Aperture antennas, patches and measurement
schedule.exercise: Size a parabolic dish for a given gain at 4 GHz, work out the dimensions of a patch antenna at 2.4 GHz on FR4, and describe how to measure a radiation pattern.

tasks.title: Compute gain, beamwidth and effective area of a parabolic reflector for dish diameters 0.6 m to 3 m at 12 GHz and tabulate the results
Apply patch design equations for a 2.4 GHz rectangular microstrip antenna on FR4, then plot return loss across frequency and read the bandwidth
Choose antennas for a village broadband site from a case file with terrain, budget and regulator constraints, and justify the gain, polarisation and mast height against the rubric

schedule.title: Free-space and terrestrial propagation
schedule.exercise: Compute free-space path loss at 900 MHz and 2.4 GHz over 5 km, compare it with an empirical macro-cell prediction for a rural area, and compute the fade margin for 99.9 percent availability.

tasks.title: Compute free-space path loss with the Friis equation for 868 MHz, 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz over distances 100 m to 20 km, and plot all three
Fit a log-distance path-loss exponent and shadowing deviation to a given set of measured received-power readings, and compare with an empirical macro-cell model
Monte Carlo simulate Rayleigh fading over 100,000 samples, find the fraction of time the signal drops 20 dB below the mean, and compare with theory

schedule.title: Microwave, satellite links and link budgets
schedule.exercise: Design a 30 km microwave hop between two hills, checking Fresnel clearance, and compute a VSAT downlink budget with rain fade for Accra.

tasks.title: Compute earth bulge and first Fresnel zone radius along a 30 km path from an elevation profile, and decide the minimum tower heights
Build a complete link budget for a 5 GHz point-to-point link, listing transmit power, gains, losses, noise and margin, and test if the link closes
Compute Eb/N0 and bit error rate for a satellite downlink across rain-attenuation values, and find the largest rain fade the link can tolerate

schedule.title: RF circuits and systems
schedule.exercise: Compute the cascaded noise figure and sensitivity of a receiver with a given filter, LNA and mixer, and find the input level at which a given amplifier reaches 1 dB compression.

tasks.title: Compute cascaded gain and noise figure for a filter, LNA and mixer chain, then see how swapping the order changes the total noise figure
Read S11, S21 and S22 from a given S-parameter table, convert S11 to return loss and VSWR, and judge whether the amplifier is matched at 2 GHz
Simulate a two-tone test on a nonlinear amplifier, measure third-order products, and extract the 1 dB compression point and IP3 from a power sweep

schedule.title: Electromagnetic compatibility and project
schedule.exercise: Review a given product for EMC risks, choosing shielding, grounding and filters, and present your link or board design project with its measured or simulated results.

tasks.title: Model capacitive coupling between a noisy switching line and a victim line, measure induced noise, and add a ground guard trace to cut it
Compute shielding effectiveness of an enclosure for absorption and reflection loss at 100 MHz and 1 GHz, and the effect of a slot aperture
Investigate a case where a mobile mast near a clinic disrupts medical equipment: gather evidence, choose mitigations and justify them against the rubric
